historical_reviews.v3_1: Preserves the two-stage oracle—non-default persistence first, then defaults matching SPEC—without permitting random or unbounded mutation.

original_test_intent: Validate that a controlled set of BIOS options can persist approved non-default values, then that Load Default restores each in-scope option to the authoritative platform specification while reboot and logs remain healthy.
original_method: Define safe reversible options and original/alternate/default values, back up configuration, apply and verify the non-default set across reboot, invoke Load Default under supervision, save/reboot, compare every in-scope field to SPEC, automate health/log checks, and restore or accept the final state explicitly.
manual_activity: An engineer must apply the controlled options, operate Load Default and supervise save/reboot transitions; the agent may compare supplied configuration exports and collect host/BMC/log health after each stage.
required_inputs: Exact host/console, BIOS build and function/page
Approved controlled option list with baseline, alternate and SPEC-default values
Complete configuration backup and validated pre-OS capture
Maintenance window, stable power, independent OOB recovery and approval for every save/reboot/default action
safety_requirements: Never mutate all or random settings
Exclude boot/security/storage/network/power options unless separately authorized
Stop on unexpected defaults, prompts, logs or boot state
Preserve logs rather than clearing baseline evidence
Restore or explicitly accept final state
No automatic retry or hardware PASS claim
agent_execution_scope: Verify supplied option matrix, SPEC and backup evidence
Prepare field-level comparison and stage identifiers
Collect read-only host/BMC/OS/SEL health before and after engineer actions
Report without operating BIOS or deciding PASS/FAIL
engineer_actions: Approve matrix, defaults oracle and recovery
Perform non-default changes and persistence reboot
Invoke Load Default and supervise save/reboot
Verify/restore or accept final configuration and own final verdict

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Correctly rejects SSH-only execution but incorrectly treats all evidence as manual; configuration comparisons and health/log collection can be automated after operator actions.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Execute the owner-approved two-stage BIOS workflow and use project-standard read-only inventory/log collection plus field-level configuration diff at each checkpoint.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Non-default persistence, Load Default, two save/reboot validations, SPEC comparison and 5/5-minute source timing are retained; unsafe all/random selection is constrained.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use unique evidence IDs for baseline, alternate persisted, default applied and final accepted/restored states, with complete field diffs and boot-health correlation.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Replaces random mutation with an auditable allowlist and makes SPEC comparison machine-checkable where exports exist.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: The source function's default behavior remains covered; unbounded random settings are not claimed as valid coverage.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Load Default may change hidden or dependent options outside the visible page and can affect boot-critical state.

project_override_considerations: The project must define the in-scope matrix and SPEC revision. Any excluded fields or owner-accepted final defaults must be reported explicitly rather than treated as full-page coverage.
expected_evidence: Host/console/row, board and BIOS build identity
Controlled option matrix with baseline/alternate/default SPEC values
Complete backup, approvals, workload state and recovery readiness
Field-level final-versus-SPEC and unrelated-setting configuration diff
Automated OS/BMC/SEL/boot health at each stage
Restored or explicitly accepted final state

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Procedure and Criteria align on persistence followed by default restoration and SPEC comparison. 'All/random' is unsafe underspecification handled as a required controlled matrix.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The option matrix, SPEC, backup and recovery are finite owner inputs; missing them requires confirmation but does not erase the clear default-restoration purpose.

review_improvement: Preserves both persistence and default-oracle stages while eliminating random broad mutation and adding auditable configuration diffs, health evidence and recovery.
independent_technical_reasoning: Load Default is a broad supervised BIOS action, but its configuration comparisons and post-reboot health checks provide substantial automatable work. With finite owner inputs and approval, REQUIRES is more accurate than MANUAL ONLY or BLOCKED.
